agentope · tool_choice · target: policies.py:lookup_when_order_number
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Evidence level   L2 Sampled (N=64, α=0.5)
Decisions        12,000   (rewarded 12,000 · expired 0 · 0.0%)

Logging policy   0.637  realized mean outcome
Target policy    0.711  SNIPS   (IPS 0.755)
Difference      +0.074  95% CI [+0.058, +0.090]

Diagnostics      ESS 3,625 (30% of n) · max weight 44 · min propensity 0.00758
                 support violations 0.1% of target mass (15 decisions) [checked against actions the logging model never produced in samples]
                 logged choice reproduced in samples: 100% · 208 decisions with < 3 matching samples

Verdict          ok

This estimate assumes:
  • The stored inputs are everything the model saw (system prompt, history, tool definitions, retrieved documents)
  • The logging model (qwen2.5-7b-instruct) behaves today as it did when logging; the logged choice came up again in samples on 100% of decisions
  • 64 samples per decision (smoothing α=0.5) estimate the propensities well enough; 208 decisions saw the logged choice fewer than 3 times
  • Which tool is called matters, not its arguments or wording (action map: tool)
  • Only tool_choice changes; later steps behave as they did under the logging policy
  • An outcome missing within 3d means outcome = 0

To strengthen this:
  • Sample more per decision (agentope sample --n 128) to firm up propensities
  • The target puts 0.1% of its probability on actions the logging policy never takes; sample more per decision, or keep the target within what the model does

Verdict          weak

This estimate assumes:
  • Every input that influenced both the logging choice and the outcome is in context (3 features: customer_tier, has_order_number, intent). Not checkable from data
  • The propensity model (multinomial logit) describes the logging policy well (see calibration above)
  • The interval treats the estimated propensities as fixed
  • Which tool is called matters, not its arguments or wording (action map: tool)
  • Only tool_choice changes; later steps behave as they did under the logging policy
  • An outcome missing within 3d means outcome = 0

To strengthen this:
  • Log with agentope.explore (ε=0.05) for ~5 weeks → Level 1 at this traffic level (aiming for ESS ≈ 400)
  • Record more of what the agent saw in context; Level 3 is only as good as context
  • If content capture is on, sample the logging model (agentope sample) → Level 2

refused.output:
agentope: refused

Level 3 (Estimated) needs your explicit acceptance of an assumption that cannot be checked.

At Level 3, agentope models how the logging policy chose from `context`.
That is only valid if every input that influenced both the
agent's choice and the outcome is recorded in `context`. Anything the agent saw
that is not in `context` (retrieved documents, conversation tone, ...) can bias
the result in either direction, and nothing in the data can reveal it.

Re-run with --accept-unverifiable (CLI) or accept_unverifiable=True (Python) to
proceed, or log with agentope.explore / agentope.randomize to reach Level 1.
